Connect the purchase to the person.

Show PayTrace how your store names its purchase fields. Confirm the mapping, prove a sandbox capture matches, then let your store report new purchases.

01 / STORE EVENTNo buyer values sent to AI

Paste one store purchase event

Use a fictional event to explore. To activate, replace the sample with an event from a completed PayPal sandbox order. Before checkout, your store server must register a purchase intent and place its returned paypalCustomId in the PayPal order’s custom_id.

AI receives field paths and data types only. Sample values, buyer details, and PayPal IDs stay out of the model request.

03 / TRUSTED ACTIVATION

Prove the payment before listening for events.

Activation rereads the PayPal sandbox order and completed capture. A matching capture proves this mapping against one purchase; it does not create a case, grant access, or prove future events. Every later event is reread separately.

SAFE PREVIEW

What PayTrace understood

STORE SERVER HANDOFF

Send future events from your server

Before each checkout, register the purchase through POST /api/intake/intent from your store server and use its returned paypalCustomId. After activation and capture, send the same event shape to POST /api/intake/event with your private store key. Browser calls are rejected. PayTrace maps the event, rereads PayPal, and creates one case only if the capture matches.

POST /api/intake/event
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_PRIVATE_STORE_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ your saved store event JSON }
Manage the store key in Connections ↗Read the integration contract ↗
PayTrace never treats a mapped store event or an AI suggestion as payment proof. Access remains subject to the merchant policy or case approval and fresh verification.
